idiom_name: opaque generator struct plus bool next(Gen *, T *) state machine
implementation_notes: C has no generator construct and no suspension, so the producer is a hand-written state machine: put the algorithm's state in a struct that an init function fills, advance it with a bool next(Gen *g, T *out) function that returns false when the sequence is exhausted, and let the loop body become the code between two suspensions. Where the natural producer shape is recursive (tree walks) or ordering must stay hidden, invert control with a callback - void gen_each(Gen *g, bool (*visit)(T, void *ud), void *ud) with a false return meaning stop - which removes the state machine at the cost of a push-style API. Reserve stackful-coroutine emulation for cases where the state machine becomes genuinely unreadable.
pitfalls: next() does not transfer ownership: handing out pointers into the generator's own buffer invalidates the previous element, so callers that store it alias later values - copy, or hand out into a caller-provided buffer.

The struct has no destructor semantics: files, statements (for example a sqlite3_stmt) or mutexes opened for the sequence must be released by an explicit gen_close() the consumer remembers to call, because C has no finally and no GC.

Exhaustion must be a distinct, sticky state: calling next() after false should keep returning false, and smuggling sentinels into payloads (0, -1, NULL) makes the generator unusable for data that contains them.

variants.name: Stackful coroutine generator (ucontext, libdill-style)
variants.idiom_name: ucontext/makecontext/swapcontext (or a libdill-style coroutine library) behind a next() API
variants.implementation_notes: A coroutine emulation gives the producer a real suspended stack, so the algorithm stays straight-line code: allocate a stack, makecontext() the producing function, and swapcontext() to it on every next() call; libdill and libco wrap the same mechanism portably. Choose it only when the state machine would be out of proportion - deep recursive producers, many interleaved sources, or existing coroutine infrastructure - and never in a signal handler or a hard-real-time path.
pitfalls: ucontext is POSIX-specific, marked obsolete in POSIX.1-2008 and deprecated on macOS, so the realization is not portable the way the state machine is; a coroutine library adds a third-party dependency.

Stack size is chosen by hand and overflow corrupts memory silently (no guard page in the base API), and no C API can unwind the coroutine stack for you, so every resource the producer holds must be released by explicit cleanup paths.
